title: Decomposing SGD Dynamics in Neural Networks: Teacher-Induced Spikes and Variance Inflation
claim: Accumulated teacher-induced structure yields a bulk-plus-spike spectrum, so a small set of outlier eigenvalues sits apart from an otherwise isotropic bulk.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right; log-scale plots, with boxed 'spikes' callouts in the two histograms
description: Three log-scale plots sit side by side, each captioned beneath. Panel (a) is a line plot of Frobenius norm against input dimension n (10^2 to 10^3). It has four curves with different markers: a solid blue starred curve for ||C_t||_F, a dotted orange curve for the summed rank-one terms, and dashed pink and dash-dotted yellow curves that decay lower. Panel (b) is a spectral density histogram of nC_t. A red bulk sits near eigenvalue 1 to 2, and a gray-outlined box labelled 'spikes' marks isolated outlier eigenvalues near 10 and 100. Panel (c) is a blue histogram of the complement Gram spectrum n_perp G_t. A dashed red Marchenko-Pastur curve fits the bulk, and a boxed spikes region lies at large eigenvalues. Legends use math notation. The eye goes first to the blue and red bulks and the spike boxes.
caption: Visualization of Lemma [ref] and Lemma [ref]. Panels (a)--(b) illustrate how the accumulation of teacher-induced structure, captured by the driver accumulator $C_t$ in [ref], leads to bulk-plus-spike behavior in its spectral density, in line with Lemma [ref]. Panel (c) shows the resulting bulk-plus-spike structure in the spectrum of $n_\perp G_t$, in line with Remark [ref]. Norms in (a) are unnormalized, and panels (a)--(b) use the realized $\mu_s\mu_s^\top$ in place of $S_s$. Parameters are $\alpha = 1.0$, $\tau = 2.0$, $\lambda = 0.01$, $k_\star = 1$, $g(\cdot) = \tanh(\cdot)$, $\sigma=\mathrm{ReLU}$, and $\eta_a = \eta_f = 0.8$ throughout, with input dimension $n=1000$ for panels (b)--(c).
abstract: We study two-layer neural networks trained by stochastic gradient descent (SGD) on a multi-index teacher model, focusing on how first-layer parameters orthogonal to the teacher subspace affect generalization. We decompose the first-layer weights into a signal component aligned with the teacher and an orthogonal complement, and analyze their joint SGD dynamics together with the second layer in the proportional limit. We show that although SGD updates to the complement are initially isotropic, the training dynamics induce teacher-dependent spectral spikes in the complement Gram matrix. This emergent anisotropy provides a concrete mechanism by which representation variance is amplified, and generalization degrades. To isolate this effect, we introduce Decomposed Dynamics, an analytically tractable surrogate whose asymptotic test-error dynamics coincide with those of SGD. In simulations with a ReLU student, freezing the directions of the orthogonal complement improves generalization relative to training them. Finally, we show that the signal component rapidly aligns with the second-layer weights, revealing strong cross-layer coupling even in this shallow setting. Together, our results provide a dynamical explanation for how feature learning outside the teacher subspace harms generalization.
